message_template: Describe the need or desired outcome before publication.
rationale: A market request cannot be interpreted or structured without a defined need.

message_template: Select the RFx request family that governs the request structure and endpoint.
rationale: RFI, RFQ, RFP, qualification, supplier, teaming, and site-selection requests require different response and decision behavior.

message_template: Establish the organization and authorized user responsible for issuing this request.
rationale: Only an authorized organization should publish a request or represent an issuer decision.

message_template: Select the governance profile and authoritative submission boundary.
rationale: The platform must know whether the transaction is private, public, institutional, external-system, or confidential site-selection activity.

message_template: Define the delivery, performance, service, or project geography.
rationale: Geography affects discovery, matching, service territory, and responder interpretation.

message_template: Set a response deadline later than publication and any required preceding events.
rationale: Responders need a valid and unambiguous submission window.

message_template: Move the question deadline before the response deadline.
rationale: Questions and resulting controlled changes must be resolved before final submission.

message_template: Add at least one structured capability, qualification, specification, commercial, or site requirement.
rationale: Structured requirements drive matching, response planning, readiness, and evaluation.

preferred_label: Capability terms are canonical or explicitly provisional
message_template: Map each mandatory capability to an active AMACS capability or resolve its provisional status.
rationale: Unreviewed free text cannot independently satisfy a hard matching gate.

message_template: Select a controlled AMACS unit for each numeric, currency, duration, distance, area, or capacity qualifier.
rationale: A numeric value without a unit cannot be compared reliably.

preferred_label: Mandatory requirement has a decision treatment
message_template: Choose whether each mandatory requirement is a gate, scored factor, gate plus scored depth, or informational item.
rationale: Requirements must remain connected to the decision architecture.

message_template: Confirm whether each capability requirement may be satisfied by an accepted teammate.
rationale: Explicit team coverage prevents an unstated assumption from changing eligibility or match explanations.

message_template: Select a response architecture template or approved custom architecture.
rationale: Responders need an ordered, complete statement of what information must be supplied.

message_template: Complete the instructions for every required response section.
rationale: A section title alone may not tell a responder what evidence, format, or limits apply.

message_template: Define whether each section may be assigned to the lead, an internal contributor, or an accepted teammate.
rationale: Ownership rules support collaborative response planning without implying that a platform invitation forms a legal agreement.

message_template: Select a decision architecture or approved custom decision process.
rationale: The issuer should establish the decision method before publication.

message_template: Adjust weighted decision factors so the total equals 100 percent.
rationale: A weighted model is not interpretable when its disclosed factor weights do not reconcile.

preferred_label: Decision factor has an evidence source
message_template: Link every comparative decision factor to at least one requirement, response section, or structured data field.
rationale: Evaluators need a disclosed source of evidence for each factor.

preferred_label: Scored capability requirements use capability fit
message_template: Add or link the Capability fit and depth factor for capability requirements scored beyond minimum coverage.
rationale: A capability requirement marked for comparative scoring must be represented in the decision architecture.

preferred_label: Gate and score do not duplicate the same fact
message_template: Review criteria that appear to award points for the same fact already used as a pass/fail gate.
rationale: Minimum compliance and comparative depth may both be used, but the identical fact should not be counted twice.

preferred_label: Requested price has a disclosed treatment
message_template: Add a price or cost factor, or explicitly mark requested pricing as informational.
rationale: Requesting price without explaining its decision treatment creates ambiguity for responders and evaluators.

message_template: Link each required response section to a requirement, readiness obligation, or decision factor.
rationale: The platform should not burden responders with required material that has no identified use.

message_template: Resolve missing, inaccessible, quarantined, or unauthorized attachments.
rationale: A published RFx must not depend on material that responders cannot access.

message_template: State whether submission occurs in The RFxchange or an authoritative external system.
rationale: The platform must never falsely represent completion of an external formal submission.

preferred_label: Information-only request has a non-award endpoint
message_template: Replace the award endpoint with information review, source identification, shortlist, connection, or another appropriate conclusion.
rationale: An RFI, Sources Sought, qualifications request, teaming request, or site-selection RFI does not automatically end in a procurement award.

message_template: Configure coded identity, invited participation, and access controls for the location project.
rationale: Site-selection projects commonly require controlled project and candidate information throughout staged evaluation.

preferred_label: Site data include units and source dates
message_template: Add the controlled unit and source date for each quantitative site, utility, workforce, infrastructure, and cost value.
rationale: Location comparisons require comparable units and time-specific data provenance.

message_template: Confirm the authority and assigned sections of each EDO, locality, utility, property, workforce, or other project contributor.
rationale: A multi-party community response needs explicit ownership and access boundaries.

message_template: Display the authoritative external submission destination and platform limitation notice.
rationale: Users must understand that preparation activity in The RFxchange is not authoritative submission or receipt.

message_template: Resolve every blocking publication-readiness finding before publishing.
rationale: Publication is the controlled transition that activates matching, notifications, response timelines, and the auditable RFx lifecycle.
